{"id": "45385231-3c89-4063-973a-e78fd5c57094", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_TXLamRd0iBF17xiMqaKTkC", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"Find the changes that could explain the symptoms, or confirm whether and when a specific change happened.\\\\n\\\\n## CloudTrail: `lookup_cloudtrail_events`\\\\n\\\\nCloudTrail calls through `use_aws` are blocked; `lookup_cloudtrail_events` is the route. It returns management events from the last 90 days, newest first, for one account and region per call.\\\\n\\\\n- Each call returns at most about 10,000 characters of events. Every event carries its full CloudTrailEvent JSON, so a call often holds only a handful of events. When it stops early it returns `continuation_timestamp`; pass that as the next `end_time` to page to older events.\\\\n- With no attribute, the tool returns only write events (`ReadOnly` is `false`), which is what a change timeline needs. LookupEvents takes one attribute per call, so passing `attribute_key` and `attribute_value` (EventSource, ResourceName, Username, EventName and so on) replaces that default, and read-only calls then share the size cap with the writes. Use an attribute to follow one resource, user or event name.\\\\n- Narrow before you page: exclude noisy event names and use windows of about 15 minutes. Excluded events do not count toward the size cap. `jmespath_filter` runs after the cap, so it shrinks the output but does not return more events.\\\\n- Passing `exclude_event_names` replaces the default exclusions (`CreateLogStream`, `Invoke`, `InvokeExecution`, `UpdateInstanceInformation`, `PutObject`); include them again if you still want them dropped.\\\\n- LookupEvents allows 2 requests per second per account and region, and one tool call may page several times, so run at most 2 CloudTrail calls at once.\\\\n- Start near the symptom onset and work backward until you find changes that address the question or have covered the requested timeframe.\\\\n\\\\nKubernetes events come from `use_kubectl`. RDS `describe_events` covers only the last 14 days; for an older window, use CloudTrail.\\\\n\\\\n## Judging a change\\\\n\\\\nA change during the incident window matters only if it relates to the investigative question or explains a symptom. When a change modified a resource that is now degraded, describe the resulting state, not just the event, and say whether that state deterministically stops the resource from working (an emptied security group, revoked IAM permissions, a black-hole route). A deterministic block takes precedence over load-based explanations, and timing alone is no reason to dismiss it.\\\\n\\\\nStop when the question is settled: you have found changes that address it, or you have covered the requested timeframe without finding any, in which case say what you searched.\\\\n\\\\nRecord each relevant change with `write_activity_observation`, including the event count and the timespan covered, unless your instructions have you state findings in your own reasoning instead.\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"references/azure.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_RZ8WKZ4eC7hu0sOFFaqGvg", "content": "[{'text': '{\"complete\":true,\"counts_scope\":\"all_associations\",\"total_count\":1,\"aws_account_count\":1,\"aws_account_counts_by_type\":{\"monitor\":1},\"aws_association_counts_by_status\":{\"valid\":1},\"aws_association_counts_by_elevated_role_status\":{},\"non_aws_count\":0,\"non_aws_counts_by_service\":{},\"non_aws_counts_by_status\":{},\"duplicate_aws_associations_collapsed\":0,\"next_token\":null,\"aws_account_row_format\":[\"accountId\",\"associationId\",\"...more associationIds for the same account\"],\"aws_accounts\":[{\"serviceId\":\"aws\",\"accountType\":\"monitor\",\"status\":\"valid\",\"count\":1,\"accounts\":[[\"012345678901\",\"4cb6eabb-aec4-4cdf-ad2d-d96cbd3319be\"]]}],\"aws_account_details\":{},\"non_aws_associations\":[]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}
